title: Hosted API - embeddings + rerank demo (Skyline)
summary: Redwood AE+SE demo of hosted embeddings + rerank endpoints for Skyline's search relevance use case. Covered API endpoints, Console walkthrough for relevance tuning, Optimize suggestions (batching/caching/quantization), security questions (VPC, SOC2, SSO), and next steps to run a benchmark POC. Customer priorities: improve relevance for e-commerce product search, keep latency <120ms for top-k rerank, and ensure data residency and audit logs.
transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2028-02-14
Start time: 16:00 PST
Duration: ~40 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Samira Patel (Redwood SE), Jordan Li (Redwood Product); Maya Torres (Skyline Eng Mgr), Tom Nguyen (Data Eng), Priya Rao (PM)

[00:00] Alex (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, happy Valentine's day if you celebrate, quick intros — I'm Alex from Redwood on the account side, Samira is our solutions engineer, Jordan product. How's everyone doing?
[00:10] Maya (Skyline): Doing well, thanks, excited to see the demo. We sent some sample queries earlier, I hope you had a chance to look.
[00:18] Samira (Redwood SE): Yep, we pulled the sample index and a few query logs, thanks for those — they were really helpful. Quick agenda: show hosted embeddings, the rerank endpoint for semantic re-ranking, then Console + Optimize suggestions and Q&A.
[00:30] Tom (Skyline): Great. Our main goals are improving search relevance for product catalogs, and keeping top-k latency under 120 ms end-to-end. Also need to confirm data controls — we have EU data residency and SOC2 requirements.
[00:42] Alex: Perfect, we'll cover both. Samira, take it away.
[00:46] Samira: Cool. I'm going to share my screen — let me know if you can't see it. (screen shares) Alright, starting with the embeddings endpoint. So the hosted flow is simple: POST to /v1/embeddings with your document payload, we return vectors, you store them in your vector DB — we can also host vectors if you want. Example request here, small code snippet in Python.
[01:12] Maya: Quick Q: do you persist the raw text on Redwood side? We want to avoid raw PII persisting.
[01:20] Jordan (Product): By default hosted API is ephemeral for request text, we have options for ingestion where customers can opt-in to vector storage; otherwise we do not persist customer doc text. For Private deployments you can keep everything in your VPC.
[01:32] Tom: And audit logs? We need an audit trail of who requested what.
[01:36] Alex: We have audit logs in the Console as an add-on, plus per-request metadata in the API logs. We can push logs to your SIEM via Syslog or S3 export.
[01:46] Samira: Back to embeddings — here's the sample response, 768-d vector example, note that the naming of dims depends on model. For Skyline we recommended a 1536-d model for product semantics given your earlier dataset size.
[02:05] Maya: You mentioned we can host vectors — pros/cons?
[02:09] Samira: If we host, no extra infra for you and we can provide built-in TTLs and vector lifecycle. If you prefer full control you can push to your Faiss/Pinecone/Weaviate; many customers use Redwood to generate embeddings and manage rerank in your stack.
[02:25] Priya (Skyline): We're leaning to keep vectors in-house for compliance but let Redwood do the embedding calls.
[02:31] Samira: That's a common pattern. Next — rerank endpoint. The flow: retrieve top-N via your vector DB or keyword, then POST candidates + query to /v1/rerank and we score / reorder. This reduces API usage compared to doing a full cross-encoder over your corpus and keeps latency low.
[02:50] Tom: What are typical latencies for rerank? We're aiming 50–120ms for a top-10 rerank.
[02:58] Samira: On hosted we can hit sub-100ms for small k on optimized kernels with batching disabled, often 40–190ms depending on model and sequence lengths. For consistent SLOs, Dedicated pools are recommended.
[03:12] Alex: Also we have automatic fallback to smaller model variants if load spikes, which helps availability.
[03:18] Maya: Any quantization impact on quality? We need to preserve relevance.
[03:22] Samira: Good question. Redwood Optimize will recommend quantization profiles per workload; typically int8 gives big cost wins with minimal delta on rerank scores, but we'll run evals on your test set to measure.
[03:36] [04:00] Samira: I'm going to demo a live rerank now. I'm switching to Console -> API Playground. You'll see a saved demo route called "Skyline - rerank demo".
[04:10] [04:18] Samira (on-screen): Here's the request: topCandidates: 10, query: "waterproof hiking jacket men", candidates text + embeds included. Hitting rerank... (typing) here's the returned scores and the reordered list. You can see how the vendor-brand noisy results drop lower.
[04:40] Priya: The ordering looks much better for long-tail queries, nice.
[04:44] Tom: Does the rerank endpoint accept embeddings directly or do you require raw text?
[04:49] Samira: We accept both: you can pass candidate embeddings or raw text; if you pass embeddings we skip tokenization which saves latency. Passing embeddings is preferred if you already have them.
[04:59] [05:10] Maya: About throughput — we have peak traffic during promotions with spikes. How do you handle bursts?
[05:18] Jordan: Hosted supports burst capacity and autoscaling; Dedicated provides reserved capacity with predictable throughput. For bursts we can configure burst pools or route to cheaper fallbacks.
[05:30] Tom: Any cold-start concerns with KV cache? I saw mention of KV cache in your docs.
[05:35] Samira: KV cache is primarily for generative workloads where you maintain long contexts. For rerank it's less important. There is a prefix cache that helps repeated queries; Redwood's batching and prefix caching optimize repeated similar requests.
[05:50] [06:05] Alex: Quick pivot to security: SOC2 is in place, we can provide the report under NDA. We support SAML 2.0/SSO, RBAC, and customer-managed KMS for key encryption in Dedicated/Private. For hosted customers we provide envelope encryption with our KMS but can integrate with your cloud KMS for Private.
[06:28] Priya: EU data residency — can we ensure embeddings never leave EU?
[06:33] Alex: Yes, we have EU regions and can pin routing so requests are processed in the EU. For extra guarantees we recommend Private (VPC) or on-prem.
[06:45] Maya: Awesome. Back to relevance testing — what does the eval workflow look like?
[06:50] Samira: We run A/B evals via Redwood Console: you can upload labeled prompts and relevance judgments; we compare models, quantization, rerank thresholds and output precision@k, MRR, etc. We can run automatic regressions alerts tied to your baseline.
[07:05] [07:30] Samira: Now opening the Optimize tab — we already ran a quick profile on your sample traffic. Here are suggestions: reduce prompt tokens, enable batching for embeddings ingestion, use int8 quantization for rerank models, and set caching TTL for repeated queries. Each suggestion has estimated cost savings.
[07:48] Tom: For batching embeddings ingestion, any guidance on batch sizes to avoid latency spikes in real-time ingestion?
[07:55] Samira: For near-real-time batch 32–64 is typical; background bulk runs can be larger. Optimize gives recommended batch sizes per throughput.
[08:05] Priya: You mentioned regressions — can we pin a model and do canary rollouts?
[08:09] Jordan: Yes, Console supports pinning, canary percentage rollouts, and automatic rollback if metrics degrade.
[08:16] [08:30] Maya: Cost — can you ballpark cost for our monthly query volume (approx 10M queries, avg top-10 rerank, embedding per doc ingestion)?
[08:38] Alex: We'll follow up with a detailed cost estimate but rough math: embedding unit cost + rerank per-call compute. Given volume you'd likely benefit from Reserved/Dedicated discounts. We'll send a model with cost scenarios.
[08:54] [09:10] Samira: Back to the demo, I'm showing the API Playground example request/response. Note the per-token cost breakdown in Console (this is new in the Cost tab). You can view token-level cost by route.
[09:28] Tom: Any issues with tokenization differences between models and our text normalization?
[09:33] Samira: We recommend preprocessing to canonicalize SKUs and strip HTML. The rerank model is somewhat robust but consistent tokenization helps. We can share a normalization guide.
[09:46] [10:00] Maya: Competitors we're evaluating are Pinecone + OpenAI, and a self-hosted cross-encoder.
[10:07] Alex: Noted — Redwood differentiators here are the unified runtime, cost controls, and built-in Optimize suggestions to tune batching/quant. We can integrate with Pinecone as your vector store.
[10:20] [10:30] Priya: Any limits on candidate size or sequence length for rerank?
[10:34] Samira: Max token length varies by model; we recommend truncating product descriptions to 512 tokens for rerank. Candidate count for top-N typically 50 or below for latency targets; we often do 10–30.
[10:48] [11:00] Samira: I'm going to run a quick live benchmark on the sample set — this will simulate top-10 rerank on 100 queries and show latency distribution. (runs benchmark) Results: p50 72ms, p95 142ms, p99 220ms on the hosted sandbox — production numbers will vary.
[11:28] Tom: p95 142ms is slightly above our 120ms target. How do we get that down?
[11:33] Samira: Options: 1) reduce model or use a smaller rerank variant, 2) move rerank to Dedicated to get lower variance, 3) pre-compute embeddings and pass to rerank to skip tokenization, 4) tune candidate size. We'll run targeted benchmarks to measure tradeoffs.
[11:52] Maya: Good — we want to see a tradeoff matrix for quality vs latency/cost.
[11:58] Samira: We'll produce that.
[12:05] [12:30] Alex: Quick note on SLOs — hosted has best-effort with burst handling; Dedicated gets SLA-backed latency/uptime. For enterprise contracts we include support windows and runbooks.
[12:46] Priya: Any compliance paperwork? SOC2, ISO?
[12:50] Alex: Yes, SOC2 Type II and ISO27001 reports available under NDA. We can include that in the security pack.
[13:00] [13:15] Maya: Ok let's document next steps.
[13:18] Alex: I'll recap then. Proposed next steps: Redwood to run benchmark POC using Skyline's 1k labeled queries (you'll share), Redwood to produce quality vs latency tradeoff matrix, send pricing scenarios (hosted vs dedicated), and include security pack + SOC2. We should schedule a follow-up in two weeks to review POC results.
[13:38] Tom: Sounds good. Action items on our side: share the 1k labeled set and give API keys for sandbox.
[13:45] Priya: Also we'll loop in compliance to review security docs.
[13:50] Alex: Great. Any other questions? 
[13:54] Maya: One micro question — does Console support live A/B for search UI experiments?
[13:58] Jordan: Yes, you can route a percent of traffic to a model variant and we track metrics per route.
[14:06] (wrap-up)
[14:10] Alex: Thanks everyone, we'll send notes and next steps right after.

End transcript
